cream-canvas.$description: Cream Canvas — Page background, hero wash, elevated card shadows — the warm paper that grounds every screen

pure-paper.$description: Pure Paper — Card surfaces, product screenshot backgrounds, button fills for ghost variants — the clean layer on top of cream

linen-border.$description: Linen Border — Primary divider color, card borders, section separators — warm gray that separates without cutting

stone-mist.$description: Stone Mist — Subtle button borders, secondary dividers — a step lighter than Linen for nested separation

warm-ash.$description: Warm Ash — Shadow tint base, muted icon strokes — warm brown undertone keeps shadows on-brand

driftwood.$description: Driftwood — Muted body text, nav borders, secondary heading borders — readable but recedes

bark.$description: Bark — Body text, secondary content — warm dark gray for paragraphs and descriptions

espresso.$description: Espresso — Primary text, headings, icons, nav text, footer text, top banner — deep warm black that replaces true black throughout

amber-signal.$description: Amber Signal — Yellow action color for filled buttons, selected navigation states, and focused conversion moments.

burnished-gold.$description: Burnished Gold — Yellow accent for outlined action borders, linked labels, and lightweight interactive emphasis. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

terracotta.$description: Terracotta — Decorative accent, chart highlight, warm icon stroke — the secondary warm hue for visual punctuation

wisteria.$description: Wisteria — Soft badge background — the only cool wash in the system, used sparingly for tag differentiation

honey-wash.$description: Honey Wash — Warm badge background — amber-tinted tag fill for status and category labels

interphases-pro-variable.$description: All interface text — headings, body, nav, buttons, labels. The custom variable font's non-standard mid-weight (492) and semibold (584) create a distinctive rhythm that standard 400/500/600/700 scales can't replicate. Tight tracking (-0.022em at display) makes headlines feel set rather than typed.
